text.what: The southernmost commercial wine region on earth, and the only part of New Zealand with a true continental climate — frost in the spring, forty-degree swings in a day, schist under everything.
text.story: Vines went from 92 hectares to 1,930 in about two decades. Pinot noir takes over 80% of the plantings, which is a bet no other region of this size has made.

kin.as: More than four fifths of everything planted here.
Bannockburn, and the cellar that made the region legible abroad.
Lake Wanaka, and one of the most photographed vineyards anywhere.
The cutting that walked through customs and changed New Zealand pinot.
